| `adr.0005-repository-tooling-is-separate-from-the-product-api` | [Repository tooling is separate from the product API](architecture/decisions/0005-repository-tooling-is-separate-from-the-product-api.md) | current | Repository-internal developer tooling lives under `tools/*` as private, unscoped packages and never becomes a Nevo SpecFlow product surface by default. | `adr.0006-product-ships-as-a-single-bundled-artifact` | [The product ships as a single bundled artifact](architecture/decisions/0006-product-ships-as-a-single-bundled-artifact.md) | superseded | `@nevo/specflow` is distributed as one self-contained tarball. `nevo-repo-product` (esbuild) bundles the `nevo-specflow` entry, the internal workspace capability packages and `commander` into `dist/bin.js`, so the artifact installs with no registry and no workspace. | `adr.0007-documentation-architecture-and-taxonomy` | [Documentation architecture and taxonomy](architecture/decisions/0007-documentation-architecture-and-taxonomy.md) | current | Defines a documentation architecture that separates product behavior, durable system architecture, engineering guidance, reusable design-system knowledge, exact reference contracts, operational instructions, and an idea backlog of proposals, while using searchable scope, area, and tag metadata so discovery does not depend on folder paths alone. |

| `adr.0012-product-package-topology-and-dependency-direction` | [Product package topology and dependency direction](architecture/decisions/0012-product-package-topology-and-dependency-direction.md) | current | Nevo SpecFlow is one npm-distributed local product composed from source packages. | `adr.0013-engine-owned-commits-and-protected-branches` | [Engine-owned scoped commits and protected branches](architecture/decisions/0013-engine-owned-commits-and-protected-branches.md) | current | When Git is enabled, Specification Create commits its scaffold through one path-limited Engine commit capability that never commits on branches the project protects. | `adr.0014-feature-owned-operation-lists` | [Feature-owned operation lists over a shared operation model](architecture/decisions/0014-feature-owned-operation-lists.md) | current | Operations are a shared entity (model, journal and registry index, per-kind adapters) read through feature-owned, read-only list routes registered by one helper. Specifications exposes GET /api/specs/operations, authorized by spec view; status comes from one documented table; freshness is by polling with ETag; there is no global operations index. |
| `adr.0015-specification-manifest-as-document-registry` | [The Specification manifest is the document registry; archetypes are project-defined catalogue entries](architecture/decisions/0015-specification-manifest-as-document-registry.md) | current | specification.yaml becomes the canonical registry of a Specification's documents (stable id, path, type) and records the selected archetype with a snapshot of its requirements. Archetypes and document types are project data files (ADR 0017), not compiled into the product. Frontmatter is optional and never authoritative; files outside the registry are unclassified. Structural completeness is a computed validation result. |
| `adr.0016-engine-owned-document-commits` | [Document operations write files at once and land as Engine-owned path-limited commits through a durable queue](architecture/decisions/0016-engine-owned-document-commits.md) | current | Amended by ADR 0018 (automatic commit is opt-in, default off). Every state-changing Specification document operation writes its files and registry change to disk immediately, answers once the content is durable and its commit request is durably queued, and lands in Git later as an Engine-owned path-limited commit executed by a per-checkout queue (one active batch per checkout, batches per Specification). Queued operations of one Specification consolidate into one commit; a batch save is one commit. The dirty window between write and commit is bounded and journaled; it relaxes the clean-checkout consequence of ADR 0013 for document operations only. Protected branches and commit blockers are checked before any file is written. Extends ADR 0013. |
| `adr.0017-definitions-as-project-data` | [Definitions are project data files read from the project configuration, never compiled into the product](architecture/decisions/0017-definitions-as-project-data.md) | current | Specification archetypes, document types and every later kind of definition (task archetypes, review kinds, ...) are YAML data files under .nevo/definitions/<kind>/ in the Project Home. The Engine reads definitions only from there, through a kind registry with a schema version and a JSON Schema per kind. The product ships default definitions as seed files used only to install them into a project. Nothing archetype-related is compiled in; deleting a file removes the definition for new work and existing Specifications keep their persisted snapshot. |
| `adr.0018-engine-commit-policy-and-manual-commit` | [Engine commit policy per capability, the uncommitted-changes ledger and manual commit](architecture/decisions/0018-engine-commit-policy-and-manual-commit.md) | current | A general policy decides per Engine capability whether its edits are committed automatically (default OFF, git.commits.auto.<capability> in project config with a local override, configuration only). With it off a write completes at once as uncommitted and is recorded in a durable, owner-keyed uncommitted-changes ledger in the durable core. A manual commit is the only way the Engine commits ledger content then: a normal operation through the same commit port, lease, claim algebra and journal, path-limited to the ledger paths of a scope, with the user's message, never arbitrary user changes. Abandoning a failed batch and policy-level auto-off are the same state. Create and definitions install stay always committed. Push is out of scope. |
| `adr.0019-workflow-kernel-and-automatic-continuation` | [One workflow kernel for Specifications and Tasks, per-Task types, agent archetypes and automatic continuation](architecture/decisions/0019-workflow-kernel-and-automatic-continuation.md) | current | Specifications and Tasks run through one deterministic workflow core and differ only in their entry points. Every Task has its own type and workflow, and the Specification archetype only restricts the types. Each step names a preferred agent archetype, which holds a preferred provider and a model per provider. A transition may continue automatically. When the Engine cannot resolve the next launch, the owner gets an attention item, derived from the state and never stored, instead of asking the agent. Canonical execution state belongs in Git in the Specification's .execution/ folder (written today, committed once follow-up F04 lands); only the change journal is local. |
| `adr.0020-documentation-discovery-is-a-product-capability` | [Documentation discovery is a product capability](architecture/decisions/0020-documentation-discovery-is-a-product-capability.md) | current | Amended by ADR 0022 (workspace-scoped documentation reader). Documentation discovery is deliberately promoted into the product as `@nevo/specflow-docs`: it owns the frontmatter contract, deterministic discovery and optional semantic search, takes its taxonomy from a settings file next to the documentation, works without an initialized project, is exposed as the ordinary CLI command `nevo-specflow docs` and as the Runtime endpoint `GET /api/docs/search`, and keeps its index fresh on Runtime start and on read without a file watcher. |
| `adr.0021-product-neutral-ai-semantic-search-engine` | [Product-neutral AI semantic search engine](architecture/decisions/0021-product-neutral-ai-semantic-search-engine.md) | current | `@nevo/ai-semantic-search` is a product-neutral engine with embedding provider, chunk source and vector store ports, an OpenAI-compatible embeddings adapter with a probe, heading-aware versioned markdown chunking and hybrid BM25 + cosine ranking fused by reciprocal rank fusion. Its local index is disposable, file-backed, written atomically under a single-writer lock and rebuilt in full on any manifest mismatch; it uses no native modules and no provider SDK. |
| `adr.0022-workspace-scoped-documentation-reader` | [Workspace-scoped documentation reader](architecture/decisions/0022-workspace-scoped-documentation-reader.md) | current | Amends ADR 0020 sections 3, 5 and 6: the Runtime serves each registered workspace's documentation under /api/workspaces/:workspaceId/docs with docs.view at project scope, replacing /api/docs/*; every checkout has its own index, embedded only through the Runtime's trusted ai.embeddings; and invalid documents are skipped everywhere except docs check. The documents ADR 0020's docs.yaml path prefixes set apart are called proposals (docs.yaml key proposals). |
